speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing that. To better understand your symptoms, have you noticed any pain specifically during penetration or with deep thrusting?

speaker: Patient
text: 30-year-old female. The patient and her husband have been trying to conceive for 15 months without success. They are sexually active at least twice a week. The husband occasionally has difficulties maintaining an erection. The patient reports discomfort and pelvic floor muscle tension during attempted vaginal penetration. Diagnosed with body dysmorphic disorder three years ago. No family history of serious illness. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. No medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: That pelvic floor tension sounds significant; does the pain radiate to your lower back or abdomen, and have you noticed any unusual vaginal discharge or bleeding between periods? Additionally, given your history of trying to conceive, have you had any prior screenings for thyroid function or ovarian reserves?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Dyspareunia secondary to vaginismus and pelvic floor dysfunction.

I recommend a pelvic floor examination and a request for images of the pelvic anatomy to confirm muscle hypertonicity.
